summary: Someone who sleeps under a bed in the sukkah has not done the mitzvah. Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon tell stories that show what the Elders thought.

chunks.en: Someone who sleeps under the bed in the sukkah
chunks.st: One who sleeps beneath the bed in the sukka

chunks.en: has not done his mitzvah.
chunks.explain: The bed is like a tent between him and the s'chach.
chunks.st: did not fulfill his obligation,
chunks.stMore: because the bed constitutes a tent that serves as a barrier between him and the roofing of the sukka.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.en: we used to do this:
chunks.st: It was our custom

chunks.he: שֶׁהָיִינוּ יְשֵׁנִים תַּחַת הַמִּטָּה בִּפְנֵי הַזְּקֵנִים,
chunks.en: we would sleep under the bed in front of the Elders,
chunks.st: that we would sleep beneath the bed before the Elders

chunks.en: and they did not say anything to us.
chunks.st: and they did not say anything to us
chunks.stMore: to the effect that we are not fulfilling our obligation. Apparently, the halakhic status of the bed is not like that of a tent and it does not prevent fulfillment of the mitzva.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said,
chunks.st: § Rabbi Shimon said, contrary to the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda:

chunks.en: Once, Tavi, the servant of Rabban
chunks.st: There was an incident involving Tavi, the Canaanite slave of

chunks.en: Gamliel, was sleeping under the bed.
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel, who was sleeping beneath the bed,

words.note: The leader of the Jewish people in his time.

chunks.en: And Rabban Gamliel said to the Elders,
chunks.st: and Rabban Gamliel lightheartedly said to the Elders:

chunks.en: "Did you see my servant Tavi?
chunks.st: Did you see my slave Tavi,

chunks.en: He is a Torah scholar, and he knows
chunks.st: who is a Torah scholar and knows

words.note: A talmid chacham is a Torah scholar.

chunks.en: that servants do not have to keep the mitzvah of sukkah.
chunks.st: that slaves are exempt from the mitzva of sukka?
chunks.stMore: Since it is a positive, time-bound mitzva, Canaanite slaves, whose status with regard to this halakhic category is like that of women, are exempt from the obligation to fulfill the mitzva of sukka.

chunks.en: That is why he sleeps under the bed."
chunks.st: Therefore, he sleeps under the bed.

chunks.en: And from his words, by the way, we learned
chunks.explain: Rabban Gamliel was not trying to teach a halacha.
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon continued: And by the way, as Rabban Gamliel was not issuing a halakhic ruling, we learned

chunks.en: that someone who sleeps under the bed
chunks.st: that one who sleeps beneath the bed

chunks.en: has not done his mitzvah.
chunks.st: did not fulfill his obligation.

summary: A sukkah leaning on a bed is kosher, but Rabbi Yehuda says it must stand by itself. A sukkah with messy s'chach, or very thick s'chach, is kosher as long as it gives more shade than sun.

chunks.en: Someone who leans his sukkah on the legs of a bed,
chunks.st: One who supports his sukka on the legs of the bed,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he leans the sukka roofing on a bed,

chunks.en: it is kosher. Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: the sukka is fit. Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: אִם אֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לַעֲמֹד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ,
chunks.en: if it cannot stand up by itself,
chunks.st: If the sukka cannot stand in and of itself without support of the bed,

chunks.en: it is not kosher. A sukkah with messy s'chach,
chunks.explain: The s'chach is not even; some is higher and some lower.
chunks.st: it is unfit. A sukka that is meduvlelet
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz leaves the word untranslated; the meaning follows Bartenura.

chunks.en: and that has more shade than sun,
chunks.st: and whose shade exceeds its sunlight

chunks.en: is kosher. One with s'chach as thick as a house,
chunks.st: is fit. A sukka whose roofing is thick like a house of sorts,

chunks.en: even though
chunks.st: even though

chunks.en: the stars cannot be seen from inside it, is kosher.
chunks.st: it is so thick that the stars cannot be seen from within it, is fit.

summary: A sukkah on a wagon, boat, tree or camel is kosher. But on Yom Tov we may not climb a tree or use an animal, so we may not go up into a sukkah that needs the tree to hold it up.

chunks.en: Someone who makes his sukkah on top of a wagon
chunks.st: In the case of one who establishes his sukka at the top of the wagon

chunks.en: or on top of a ship,
chunks.st: or at the top of the ship,

chunks.en: it is kosher, and we may go up into it on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: although it is portable it is fit, as it is sufficient for a sukka to be a temporary residence. And one may ascend and enter it even on the first Festival day.

chunks.he: בְּרֹאשׁ הָאִילָן אוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי גָמָל,
chunks.en: On top of a tree or on a camel,
chunks.st: In the case of one who establishes his sukka at the top of a tree or atop a camel,

chunks.he: כְּשֵׁרָה, וְאֵין עוֹלִין לָהּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
chunks.en: it is kosher, but we may not go up into it on Yom Tov.
chunks.explain: The Rabbis said not to climb trees or use animals on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: the sukka is fit, but one may not ascend and enter it on the first Festival day
chunks.stMore: because the Sages prohibit climbing or using trees or animals on the Festival.

chunks.en: If two walls are in the tree and one is made by a person,
chunks.st: If two of the walls of the sukka are in the tree and one is established on the ground by a person,

chunks.he: אוֹ שְׁתַּיִם בִּידֵי אָדָם וְאַחַת בָּאִילָן,
chunks.en: or two are made by a person and one is in the tree,
chunks.st: or if two are established on the ground by a person and one is in the tree,

chunks.he: כְּשֵׁרָה, וְאֵין עוֹלִין לָהּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
chunks.en: it is kosher, but we may not go up into it on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: the sukka is fit, but one may not ascend and enter it on the first Festival day
chunks.stMore: because it is prohibited to use the tree.

chunks.en: If three are made by a person and one is in the tree,
chunks.st: However, if three of the walls are established on the ground by a person and one is in the tree,

chunks.en: it is kosher, and we may go up into it on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: then since it contains the minimum number of walls required, it is fit, and one may enter it on the first Festival day.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: The mishna summarizes that this is the principle:

chunks.en: any sukkah that, if the tree were taken away, could
chunks.st: Any case where, were the tree removed, the

chunks.en: stand up by itself,
chunks.st: sukka would be able to remain standing in and of itself,

chunks.en: is kosher, and we may go up into it on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: it is fit, and one may ascend and enter it on the Festival,
chunks.stMore: since the tree is not its primary support.

summary: Trees can be the walls of a sukkah. People busy with a mitzvah, sick people and those who take care of them do not have to sit in the sukkah. A small snack may be eaten outside the sukkah.

chunks.en: Someone who makes his sukkah between the trees,
chunks.st: In the case of one who establishes his sukka between the trees,

chunks.en: and the trees are its walls,
chunks.st: and the trees serve as walls for it,

chunks.he: כְּשֵׁרָה. שְׁלוּחֵי מִצְוָה פְּטוּרִין מִן הַסֻּכָּה.
chunks.en: it is kosher. People on their way to do a mitzvah do not have to sit in the sukkah.
chunks.st: the sukka is fit. Those on the path to perform a mitzva are exempt from the mitzva of sukka.

chunks.en: Sick people and those who take care of them do not have to sit in the sukkah.
chunks.st: The ill and their caretakers are exempt from the mitzva of sukka.

chunks.en: We may eat and drink a snack outside the sukkah.
chunks.explain: A small snack, not a real meal.
chunks.st: One may eat and drink in the framework of a casual meal outside the sukka.

summary: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai and Rabban Gamliel ate even a little food in the sukkah. Rabbi Tzadok ate a tiny bit of food outside the sukkah and did not make a bracha after it.
stIntro: Apropos eating in the sukka, which is discussed in the previous mishna, this mishna relates:

chunks.en: Once, they brought to Rabban Yochanan
chunks.st: An incident occurred where they brought a cooked dish to Rabban Yoḥanan

chunks.en: ben Zakkai a cooked dish to taste,
chunks.st: ben Zakkai for him to taste,

words.note: A great leader of the Jewish people after the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed.

chunks.en: and to Rabban Gamliel two dates
chunks.st: and to Rabban Gamliel they brought two dates

chunks.en: and a bucket of water.
chunks.st: and a bucket of water.

chunks.en: And they said, "Take them up to the sukkah."
chunks.st: And they each said: Take them up to the sukka

chunks.en: And when they gave Rabbi Tzadok
chunks.st: and we will eat them there. In contrast, the mishna relates: And when they gave Rabbi Tzadok

chunks.en: less than an egg's worth of food,
chunks.st: less than an egg-bulk of food,

words.en: than the size of an egg

chunks.en: he picked it up with a cloth,
chunks.explain: He did not wash his hands for such a small amount.
chunks.st: he took the food in a cloth
chunks.stMore: for cleanliness; he did not wash his hands because in his opinion, one is not required to wash his hands before eating less than an egg-bulk.

chunks.he: וַאֲכָלוֹ חוּץ לַסֻּכָּה, וְלֹא בֵרַךְ אַחֲרָיו:
chunks.en: and ate it outside the sukkah, and did not make a bracha after it.
chunks.st: And he ate it outside the sukka and did not recite a blessing after eating it.
chunks.stMore: He holds that one is not required to recite a blessing after eating less than an egg-bulk, as it is not satisfying, and it is written: “And you shall eat and be satisfied and bless the Lord your God” (Deuteronomy 8:10). The Gemara will explain the halakhic rationale for each of these actions described.

summary: Rabbi Eliezer says one must eat fourteen meals in the sukkah. The Sages say only the meal on the first night is a must. If you missed it, the Sages say it cannot be made up.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: fourteen meals a person must
chunks.st: A person is obligated to eat fourteen meals

chunks.en: eat in the sukkah,
chunks.st: in the sukka over the course of the seven days of the festival of Sukkot,

chunks.en: one in the day and one at night.
chunks.st: one during the day each day and one at night each night.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: there is no set number,
chunks.st: There is no quota
chunks.stMore: for the number of meals, and one may choose whether or not to eat any of the meals

chunks.en: except for the night of the first Yom Tov
chunks.st: except for the meal on the evening of the first Festival day

chunks.en: of the chag, only.
chunks.st: of Sukkot,
chunks.stMore: which one is required to eat in the sukka.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Eliezer also said,
chunks.st: And furthermore, Rabbi Eliezer said:

chunks.en: someone who did not eat on the night of
chunks.st: One who did not eat

chunks.en: the first Yom Tov
chunks.st: a meal on the evening of the first day of the Festival

chunks.en: should make it up on the night of the last Yom Tov.
chunks.explain: The last Yom Tov is Shemini Atzeres.
chunks.st: should compensate with a meal on the evening of the last day of the Festival, on the Eighth Day of Assembly,
chunks.stMore: despite the fact that he will not eat it in the sukka.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: there is no making it up.
chunks.st: There is no compensation for this matter,

chunks.en: About this it says:
chunks.st: and with regard to similar cases where it is impossible to rectify failure to fulfill a positive mitzva, it is stated:

chunks.en: "What is crooked cannot be made straight,
chunks.st: “That which is crooked cannot be made straight;

chunks.en: and what is missing cannot be counted."
chunks.st: and that which is wanting cannot be numbered” (Ecclesiastes 1:15).

summary: Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue about someone who sits with his head and most of his body in the sukkah while his table is in the house. They argue about a story with Rabbi Yochanan ben HaChoranis.

chunks.en: Someone whose head and most of his body were in the sukkah,
chunks.st: In the case of one whose head and most of his body were in the sukka

chunks.en: and his table was inside the house:
chunks.st: and his table was in the house,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say it is not kosher,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai deem it unfit,

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel say it is kosher.
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel deem it fit.

chunks.he: אָמְרוּ לָהֶן בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי,
chunks.en: Beis Hillel said to Beis Shammai,
chunks.st: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:

chunks.en: "Wasn't there a story like this?
chunks.st: And wasn’t there an incident

chunks.en: The Elders of Beis Shammai and the Elders of
chunks.st: where the Elders of Beit Shammai and the Elders of

chunks.en: Beis Hillel went to visit Rabbi
chunks.st: Beit Hillel went to visit Rabbi

chunks.en: Yochanan ben HaChoranis,
chunks.st: Yoḥanan ben HaḤoranit

chunks.he: וּמְצָאוּהוּ שֶׁהָיָה יוֹשֵׁב רֹאשׁוֹ וְרֻבּוֹ בַסֻּכָּה,
chunks.en: and they found him sitting with his head and most of his body in the sukkah,
chunks.st: and they found him such that he was sitting with his head and most of his body in the sukka

chunks.en: and his table inside the house,
chunks.st: and his table in the house,

chunks.en: and they did not say anything to him."
chunks.st: and they said nothing to him?
chunks.stMore: Even Beit Shammai did not object.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai said to them,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai said to them:

chunks.en: "Is that a proof?
chunks.st: Is there proof from there?
chunks.stMore: That is not what happened; rather,

chunks.en: They really said to him,
chunks.st: they said to him:

chunks.en: 'If this is how you always did it,
chunks.st: If you were accustomed to act in this manner,

chunks.en: you never kept the mitzvah of sukkah in your life!'"
chunks.st: you have never fulfilled the mitzva of sukka in your life.

summary: Women, servants and young children do not have to sit in the sukkah, but a child who no longer needs his mother must. Shammai made a sukkah over the bed for his new grandson.

chunks.en: Women, servants and young children
chunks.st: Women, slaves, and minors

chunks.en: do not have to sit in the sukkah.
chunks.st: are exempt from the mitzva of sukka.

chunks.en: A child who does not need his mother anymore
chunks.explain: He does not wake up calling for his mother.
chunks.st: A minor who does not need his mother any longer

chunks.en: must sit in the sukkah.
chunks.st: is obligated in the mitzva.

chunks.en: Once, the daughter-in-law of Shammai had a baby,
chunks.st: There was an incident where the daughter-in-law of Shammai

chunks.en: the Elder, and he broke open the plaster roof and put s'chach
chunks.st: the Elder gave birth just before Sukkot, and Shammai removed the coat of plaster from the roof, leaving the beams, and roofed with the beams

words.en: and he made a hole in

chunks.en: over the bed, for the baby.
chunks.st: over the bed for the newborn minor.

summary: During Sukkos, the sukkah is our main home. If it rains hard enough to spoil food, we may go inside. The rain is like a master who does not want his servant's service.

chunks.en: All seven days, a person makes
chunks.st: All seven days of Sukkot, a person renders

chunks.en: his sukkah his real home, and his house only for a short while.
chunks.st: his sukka his permanent residence and his house his temporary residence.

chunks.en: If rain fell,
chunks.st: If rain fell,

chunks.en: from when may he leave the sukkah?
chunks.st: from when is it permitted to vacate the sukka?

chunks.en: From when the rain would spoil a thick dish.
chunks.st: It is permitted from the point that it is raining so hard that the congealed dish will spoil.

words.note: A thick food, like porridge, that is spoiled by a little water.

chunks.en: They gave a parable:
chunks.st: The Sages told a parable:

chunks.en: what is this like?
chunks.st: To what is this matter comparable?

chunks.en: To a servant who came to pour a cup of wine for his master,
chunks.st: It is comparable to a servant who comes to pour wine for his master,

chunks.en: and his master poured a jug of water in his face.
chunks.explain: This shows the master does not want his service.
chunks.st: and he pours a jug [kiton] of water in his face to show him that his presence is not desired. So too, in the sukka, rain is an indication that the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not want the person to fulfill the mitzva of sukka.
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura says clearly that it is the master who pours the water.
